question: The Supreme Court Judges Removal motion must be signed by __________ members in the Lok Sabha or __________ members in the Rajya Sabha to adopt the motion in the parliament.
solution:
The correct answer is **1**__**00 members in the Lok Sabha and 50 members in the Rajya Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The motion for the removal of a Supreme Court Judge in India must be signed by** at least 100 members in the Lok Sabha** and **50 members in the Rajya Sabha** before being admitted.
 
• The process for the removal of Supreme Court Judges is outlined in **Article 124(4) of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• The grounds for removal are limited to** proven misbehavior or incapacity**, ensuring that judges cannot be removed arbitrarily.
 
• Once the motion is admitted, it is referred to a three-member investigative committee comprising a Supreme Court judge, a Chief Justice of a High Court, and a distinguished jurist.
 
• If the committee finds the allegations valid, the motion needs to be passed by both Houses of Parliament with a **two-thirds majority of members present and voting** before the judge can be removed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968**

 
 
• The procedure for the removal of Supreme Court Judges is governed by the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.
 
• The Act elaborates on the process after the removal motion is admitted, including the formation of an investigative committee and voting thresholds in Parliament.
 
• The removal process ensures judicial independence by safeguarding against arbitrary dismissal.
